samples.summary: `sidebar`/`split` reflow moves every text whose `frame.x < w` to the SAME x, so a two-column layout's left column lands on top of its untouched right column
samples.evidence: `if (t.frame.x < w) { const nx = w + 100; t.frame.x = nx; t.frame.w = Math.max(240, SW - nx - 128); }`. For `title-two-columns` (layout.ts:113-126) the left body is at x=80 and the right body at x = PADDING+HALF+PADDING = 1000. With `sidebar` (w=640) the left column is moved to x=740 and widened to 1052 (740→1792), so it overlaps the right column starting at 1000; with `split` (w=960) the left column moves to 1060 while the right stays at 1000, again overlapping. The rule only tests the left edge and never re-flows or narrows the sibling column, so the two bodies render on top of each other. No shipped template currently pairs `title-two-columns` with `sidebar`/`split` (all such slides use `plain`), so today it is latent — but it is one tuple away in a catalogue whose whole point is mixing presets per slide.

samples.summary: `recolor`'s `maxY` test uses only the text frame's top edge, so a box that starts inside the header band but extends past it is recoloured entirely to `background` (invisible below the band)
samples.evidence: `if (t.frame.y > maxY) continue;` — the intent (`case 'header'`: `recolor(texts, 'background', 300)` after painting an accent rect over y 0..300) is "recolour what sits on the band", but the predicate ignores `frame.h`. A placeholder at y=250 with h=400 passes the test and every inline becomes `role: 'background'`, which renders as background-on-background for the ~350px that fall outside the accent rect. The `header` preset is not used by any template in this change, so the defect is latent; the correct test is `t.frame.y + t.frame.h <= maxY`.

samples.summary: `themedDeck` silently discards `texts` entries beyond the layout's placeholder count, unlike the loud guard it sits next to for an unknown layout id
samples.evidence: `const target = placeholders[i]; if (!target) return;` — a catalogue entry that supplies three text arrays for a two-slot layout (e.g. passing `title-body` where `title-two-columns` was meant) loses the third column with no error, producing a shipped template that is missing content. The adjacent layout guard (`if (!layout) throw new Error(...)`, line 342) and the theme guard (line 332) both fail the seed on the analogous typo, so the inconsistency is deliberate only by omission. Pre-existing in `slide()` (line 126) and copied here.

samples.summary: Several brief `max` row counts exceed the number of rows the matching template slide actually provides, contradicting the documented meaning of `min`/`max`
samples.evidence: `brief.ts` documents `min`/`max` as "For `list` / `pairs`: how many rows the slide is designed for." But: `sprintRetrospectiveBrief.wentWell`/`toImprove` declare max 4 while the `sprint-retrospective` `title-body` slides ship 3 lines (slides-more.ts:32-36, 44-47); `sprintRetrospectiveBrief.actions` declares max 4 while the two-column slide ships 3 `—` rows (slides-more.ts:54-55); `okrReviewBrief.keyResults` declares max 5 against 4 rows (slides-more.ts:88-89); `productLaunchPlanBrief.channels` declares max 4 against 3 rows; `techTalkBrief.strengths`/`limitations` declare max 3 against 2 rows (slides-more.ts:200). A fill agent trusting the schema will collect more values than the slide was composed for. `briefs.spec.ts` only checks `min <= max`, never that either matches the template.
searchedFor: compared each list/pairs field's min/max against the template's line/row counts
